reproduction: Visit /systems then each /universe/* lens and diff the captured metrics
what_is_wrong: Six navigation destinations render the same page. All report exactly 92 controls, 17 cards and an identical H1>H2x6 heading structure; on-screen text differs by 38-91 characters out of 5163 — under 2%.
why_it_feels_wrong: Choosing a lens changes a label and almost nothing else, so navigation promises depth the page does not deliver
usability_impact: A user who clicks Map, Orbits, Timeline, Research and Web Signals sees the same screen five times and learns the nav is decorative
emotional_impact: Six named destinations that do not differentiate reads as a demo, not a product
brand_impact: Landmark and heading structure is identical across six routes, so screen-reader users get no signal they moved
accessibility_impact: None — the work is already rendered
performance_impact: renderWorldLens updates a sub-panel only; the surrounding 98% of the page is shared chrome that never changes per lens
root_cause: Each lens must own the primary layer: its own hero treatment, its own heading, and its own dominant data object. The shared chrome should recede when a lens is active.
recommended_direction: Any two lens routes differ by >25% of visible text and by their H1 content; heading structure differs per lens

reproduction: Measure getBoundingClientRect on every visible control
what_is_wrong: 62 of 92 visible controls are smaller than 44x44 CSS px on desktop; 19 of 70 on mobile. CORRECTION: 44x44 is Apple HIG design guidance, not a WCAG requirement. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA) requires 24x24 CSS px with a spacing exception. The count below 24x24 has NOT been measured, so no conformance failure is claimed yet.
why_it_feels_wrong: Controls feel fiddly and imprecise, which reads as cheap regardless of how the page looks
usability_impact: Mis-taps and repeated attempts on the densest surfaces
emotional_impact: Precision work feels stressful rather than effortless
brand_impact: UNPROVEN as a conformance failure until re-measured at 24x24 with the spacing exception applied; currently a design-quality finding
performance_impact: Topbar, nav and scope chips were sized for visual density, not for hit area; no shared minimum-target token exists
root_cause: Re-measure at 24x24 including the spacing exception to establish conformance. Separately adopt 44x44 as the NUR design token for touch surfaces, achieved with padding or ::before overlays without changing visual size
recommended_direction: Zero visible controls below 24x24 without satisfying the WCAG spacing exception; zero below 44x44 on touch viewports

reproduction: Measure computed fontSize on visible text nodes
what_is_wrong: Between 40 and 75 visible text elements per route render below 12px. Omega review is worst at 75; Systems 54; Today 18
why_it_feels_wrong: Sub-12px text signals "dense admin tool", which contradicts the editorial ambition of the display type
usability_impact: Provenance, telemetry and evidence lines are the hardest to read yet carry the highest trust value
emotional_impact: The most trustworthy content is the least legible
brand_impact: Below the practical legibility floor; no user-facing size control
accessibility_impact: Telemetry styling was tuned for compactness with no minimum-size rule in the type scale
performance_impact: Set a floor in the responsive type scale. Telemetry may be small and quiet but never below the floor; use opacity and letter-spacing for hierarchy instead of shrinking
root_cause: No visible text below the token floor at any viewport

reproduction: Read the captured headings string: H1>H2x6>H1>H2x5
what_is_wrong: Two H1 elements on the same page — the canonical page title plus the adjunct surface title
why_it_feels_wrong: Two competing titles means neither reads as the subject of the screen
emotional_impact: The page argues with itself about what it is
brand_impact: Two H1 landmarks break document outline for assistive technology
accessibility_impact: Adjunct surfaces render their own H1 into a canonical page that already has one
performance_impact: Adjunct surfaces should adopt H2 and inherit the canonical H1, or the canonical H1 should be suppressed when an adjunct owns the viewport
root_cause: Exactly one H1 per route at every viewport

reproduction: Count disabled visible controls per route
what_is_wrong: 14 controls are permanently disabled on every universe route; 16 on Settings
why_it_feels_wrong: Persistently dead controls teach the user that parts of the interface are decoration
usability_impact: Users repeatedly test controls that never respond
emotional_impact: A shipped product with permanently greyed controls reads as unfinished
brand_impact: Disabled state alone does not communicate why; no accessible explanation is attached
accessibility_impact: These correspond to the 7 NOT_IMPLEMENTED_VISIBLE and 2 BLOCKED_BY_EXTERNAL_PROVIDER entries in the control matrix
performance_impact: Every disabled control must carry an honest reason on focus and hover. Controls blocked by an unconfigured provider should say so; unimplemented ones should not be visible at all
root_cause: Zero disabled controls without an accessible reason; NOT_IMPLEMENTED_VISIBLE count reaches 0

reproduction: Compare control and character counts across routes
what_is_wrong: 135 controls and 11614 characters on one screen — 47% more controls and 125% more text than the Systems route
why_it_feels_wrong: Everything is present at once with no progressive disclosure, so nothing is prioritised
usability_impact: The reviewer must parse the whole screen before acting
emotional_impact: Density without hierarchy reads as an admin console
brand_impact: High cognitive load; long tab sequence
accessibility_impact: Review was built as a complete form rather than a staged decision flow
performance_impact: Stage the review: one claim at a time in the primary layer, the queue in the secondary layer, provenance in the tertiary
root_cause: No route exceeds 80 visible controls without progressive disclosure

reproduction: Compare desktop and mobile metrics per route
what_is_wrong: Mobile trims proportionally rather than recomposing: Systems drops 24% of controls and 23% of text; Omega review keeps 113 of 135 controls and 10431 of 11614 characters
why_it_feels_wrong: The mobile screen is the desktop screen with less room, not a layout designed for a phone
usability_impact: Long scrolls and small targets on the surfaces that matter most
brand_impact: Small targets and long tab sequences compound on touch
accessibility_impact: No separate mobile composition exists; layout is fluid rather than art-directed
performance_impact: Design mobile as its own composition per tier: one hero object, one primary action, telemetry moved into expandable sheets
root_cause: Mobile carries <=50% of desktop controls above the fold on every Tier A and B route

reproduction: Watch the console across a full authenticated census
what_is_wrong: One 401 Unauthorized during the authenticated session
why_it_feels_wrong: A silent authorisation failure during normal use suggests something is not wired correctly
usability_impact: No visible breakage observed, but an unexplained 401 is unexplained state
emotional_impact: Silent failures erode confidence in correctness
brand_impact: May indicate a surface that renders without its data
accessibility_impact: Not yet attributed to a specific request
performance_impact: Attribute the request, then either authorise it or stop issuing it
root_cause: Zero unexplained 4xx responses across a full authenticated census

reproduction: Count visible card and panel containers
what_is_wrong: 17 to 22 card or panel containers per route with near-uniform visual weight
why_it_feels_wrong: Equal-weight cards mean the composition never states what matters most
usability_impact: The eye has no entry point; scanning is linear
emotional_impact: Card-grid uniformity is the generic-SaaS signature the directive forbids
brand_impact: Nothing critical is conveyed by position or emphasis
accessibility_impact: The adjunct language is a responsive panel grid applied uniformly regardless of tier
performance_impact: Panels should attach to the scene and appear contextually. Tier A surfaces should carry one dominant object with 2-4 supporting metrics, not 17 equal cards
root_cause: No Tier A route shows more than 6 equal-weight containers in the initial viewport

reproduction: Compare text volume against sibling working surfaces
what_is_wrong: 6783 characters on desktop and 5760 on mobile — the highest text volume of any Tier B working surface, and mobile removes only 15%
why_it_feels_wrong: The surface where a user works longest is the one that trims least on a phone
usability_impact: Prolonged reading on the smallest screen
emotional_impact: The working surface should feel calm and does not
accessibility_impact: Talk transcript is rendered in full with no viewport-aware truncation or collapse
performance_impact: Collapse older turns behind an explicit control on mobile; keep the current exchange dominant
root_cause: Talk mobile shows <=60% of desktop text volume at first paint
